subject: Civil Engineering
title: Immersed Tube Tunnels
description: A fast breakdown of Immersed Tube Tunnels for builders.

hook.text: How do you build a tunnel under a river? Float it into place — piece by piece.

buildup.text: Massive concrete tubes are cast in a dry dock, sealed, and floated to the tunnel site.

discovery.text: A trench is dredged in the riverbed. The tubes are sunk, aligned, and joined underwater.

twist.text: Rubber gaskets between segments compress when water pressure pushes — sealing the joints.

climax.text: The Marmaray tunnel under Istanbul's Bosphorus — immersed tubes connecting Europe and Asia.

punchline.text: Sink a tunnel into place like blocks on a riverbed. That's immersed tube.

quiz.question: How are immersed tube tunnel segments installed?
options: They are bored through the riverbed using underwater TBMs
Prefabricated concrete tubes are floated, sunk into a dredged trench, and joined underwater
Divers manually assemble concrete blocks on the riverbed

details.summary: Immersed tube tunnels are constructed by prefabricating large concrete or steel tunnel sections in a dry dock, floating them to the crossing location, sinking them into a prepared trench on the waterway bed, and joining them underwater.
details.whyItMatters: Immersed tubes provide wider, shallower tunnel profiles than bored tunnels for water crossings. They are often the most practical method for road and rail crossings of navigable waterways.
takeaways: Tunnel elements are prefabricated onshore then floated into position
Elements are lowered into a dredged trench and joined using rubber gaskets
Backfill and rock armor protect the completed tunnel from anchors and erosion

faq.question: How are immersed tube tunnel sections connected underwater?
faq.answer: Each new element is floated over its position, ballasted to sink, then guided into contact with the previously placed element. A rubber gasket seal compresses as water pressure pushes the elements together. The joint is dewatered and inspected, then a permanent steel closure is welded.

faq.question: What are the advantages of immersed tubes over bored tunnels for water crossings?
faq.answer: Immersed tubes sit closer to the surface, requiring shorter approach ramps. They can be wider and flatter than circular bored tunnels, providing better road geometry. Construction quality is higher because sections are built in dry conditions. They are often cheaper for wide waterway crossings.
